title: 3.2.13 Lab: square(n)
description: Write square(n) so that it hands back n times n with return, and use the value it gives back. The first return practice. Practice, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write square
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called square that takes one parameter, n. You met square in 3.2.11; write it from memory, and look back only if you are stuck.

steps.title: Return the product
steps.instructions: Hand back n times n with return (3.2.11), not console.log. A returned value is something the rest of your program can use.

steps.title: Use what comes back
steps.instructions: Store square(5) in a variable, then console.log that variable plus 1. Getting 26 proves a real number came back.

requirements.title: square is defined with one parameter
requirements.description: Code defines a function named square with exactly one parameter. Help: 3.2.5 (Parameters and Arguments)
requirements.hint: Write function square(n) { ... } with exactly that name and one name between the parentheses.

requirements.title: square hands back a value with return
requirements.description: square contains a return statement. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: The line that produces the answer should start with return, not console.log.

requirements.title: square returns n times n
requirements.description: square(n) gives back n multiplied by itself, for any number. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: square(n) must give back n * n. An answer of 8 for 4 means you added n to itself. If the right number only appears in the output but the check says undefined, you printed it: use return.
